justifications.functional_suitability: While scheduling (Node.js Scheduling Service, Resource Clash Detector) and EMR (Go EMR Service) are addressed, R-04 (Billing & insurance claims) lacks a dedicated service or component. Billing Specialists and external payment systems are present, but the core billing processing logic is missing from the containers.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Target R-07 (<1s P95 EMR load) is achieved via React Query caching, Go EMR Service's EMR Query Handler with Redis Cluster caching, Read-Only Replica Nodes offloading traffic, and PgBouncer connection pooling to avoid database bottlenecks.
justifications.compatibility: Thoroughly meets R-08 via Apache Camel ESB, featuring FHIR Transformation Processor and Secure Protocol Adapter connecting to External Lab and Imaging Systems. Go EMR Service also contains an internal FHIR Adapter for standards compliance.
justifications.usability: All specified actors (Clinicians, Patients, Front Desk, Billing, Administrators) access the system via React Single Page Application (SPA). Router & View Controller provides persona-specific views, though serving external patients and internal clinical users through a single SPA interface represents a minor design compromise.
justifications.reliability: PostgreSQL Cluster uses a single Primary Write Node with Synchronous Standby Nodes, which contradicts the brief's active-active hybrid requirement (R-06). However, Redis Sentinel Manager and Camel Dead Letter Channel offer good component-level fault recovery. 10-year data retention is unaddressed.
justifications.security: Excellently satisfies R-05, HIPAA, and GDPR. Implements OAuth2 & MFA Authentication Module on Kong Gateway, AES-256 storage encryption, Data Masking Engine, pgaudit Extension, HashiCorp Vault Secrets Manager, and TLS 1.3/mTLS across service-to-service communication.
justifications.maintainability: Strong microservice separation across Go EMR Service and Node.js Scheduling Service, decoupled via Apache Kafka Event Bus with Schema Registry. Domain outbox pattern ensures data consistency. Maintainability is slightly reduced by the omitted billing container.
justifications.portability: Fully aligned with target hybrid environments (on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1). Employs Strimzi Operator, CloudNativePG/Patroni Orchestrator, and cloud-agnostic open-source containers (Redis, Kong, Camel, PostgreSQL) seamlessly deployable onto any standard Kubernetes cluster.

PERF-01.justification: Multi-tier caching with React Query, Redis caching in the Go EMR Query Handler, and PgBouncer connection pooling directly support sub-second P95 loads under concurrent clinician read traffic.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratios in Redis for frequently accessed patient charts
Connection pool saturation on PgBouncer under synchronized morning traffic
tradeoffs: In-memory Redis caching increases read performance but risks serving stale clinical records

PERF-02.justification: Apache Camel ESB and Kafka decouple bursty external FHIR loads from the transactional core, while read-only database replicas protect interactive EMR screen queries from write contention.
sensitivity_points: Throughput and parsing latency of FHIR Transformation Processor under burst loads
Write IOPS limits on the PostgreSQL Primary Write Node
tradeoffs: Asynchronous event ingestion protects query response times but delays immediate record visibility

AVAIL-01.justification: Patroni and synchronous standbys manage database failover, but hybrid multi-site active-active networking, cross-region split-brain handling, and global traffic routing are not defined.
sensitivity_points: Network latency and reliability across the hybrid WAN connection
Automated failover convergence speed orchestrated by Patroni
tradeoffs: Synchronous replication prevents data loss across sites but degrades write latency over hybrid links

AVAIL-02.justification: PostgreSQL provides Patroni failover for database crashes, but the architecture completely omits a billing container and claim retry orchestration mechanism to handle in-flight submissions.
sensitivity_points: Absence of a specialized billing container to manage claim state machines
Database failover time remaining strictly under the 30-second window
tradeoffs: Strict synchronous writes guarantee transactional durability but can block pending claims during failover

MOD-01.justification: The design lacks a billing service and dedicated insurance clearinghouse adapter; billing interfaces are left unmodeled at container and component levels, preventing isolated clearinghouse modifications.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between external insurance clearinghouses and unspecified internal billing workflows
Extensibility of Apache Camel ESB beyond lab and imaging systems
tradeoffs: Centralizing all integrations into Camel simplifies routing but risks monolithic integration logic

MOD-02.justification: Schema and UI additions are cleanly restricted to three components: React SPA views, Go EMR handlers, and PostgreSQL, with pgaudit automatically auditing the new field without custom code.
sensitivity_points: Schema migration overhead and table locking on the PostgreSQL Cluster
Dynamic audit coverage across newly added entity fields
tradeoffs: Dynamic field auditing via pgaudit avoids custom code but increases database log volumes

SEC-01.justification: The API Gateway's OAuth2 & MFA module enforces multi-factor authentication at perimeter ingress, stopping single-factor breaches, although a specific 1-minute alerting system is omitted.
sensitivity_points: Perimeter enforcement strictness of Lua-based MFA plugins in Kong
Timely emission and routing of failed authentication events
tradeoffs: Mandatory MFA at the perimeter stops unauthorized access but introduces friction for clinicians

SEC-02.justification: While ABAC and audit logging modules exist, ABAC is restricted to the write processor, and Redis-cached reads bypass database audit interceptors, risking unaudited chart views.
sensitivity_points: Coverage of the Audit Log Interceptor over cached read-only requests
Enforcement of ABAC relationship checks during EMR read operations
tradeoffs: Auditing every single read query prevents compliance breaches but introduces logging latency and storage overhead
